# ISO 27001:2022 Gap Analysis and Roadmap: 250-Person Fintech

**Assumptions:** cloud and on-prem mix, card data in scope for PCI DSS v4.0.1, and no dedicated GRC tooling yet. **Timeline:** 6 months is aggressive from a standing start. **9 months is realistic.** Certification bodies generally expect the ISMS to have run for about 3 months, with an internal audit and a management review completed, before Stage 2.

**Regulatory note:** If your EU customers are banks, insurers, or payment firms, they are subject to **DORA** (applies since January 2025) and will likely push ICT contract requirements down to you. Ask your key EU customers about this early, because it affects supplier, incident, and continuity work.

---

## 1. Prioritized Gap-Analysis Checklist

**Priority key:**
- **P1** = certification blocker or highest risk
- **P2** = needed before Stage 2
- **P3** = can mature after certification

### Phase 1: Foundation (Months 0–2)

**Clauses 4–6: ISMS core (all P1, all mandatory)**
- [ ] Secure an executive sponsor and name an ISMS owner (Clause 5.1, 5.3)
- [ ] Document context, interested parties, and requirements (4.1, 4.2), including GDPR, PCI DSS, customer contracts, and climate relevance (per the 2024 amendment)
- [ ] Define the **ISMS scope**, including boundaries, locations, systems, and interfaces (4.3). Consider aligning it with your PCI cardholder data environment so evidence can be reused.
- [ ] Get an information security policy approved by top management (5.2, A.5.1)
- [ ] Define roles and responsibilities with a RACI (5.3, A.5.2)
- [ ] Write a risk assessment methodology covering criteria, scales, and risk acceptance (6.1.2)
- [ ] Complete the risk assessment and produce a risk register
- [ ] Write a risk treatment plan and **Statement of Applicability** covering all 93 Annex A controls, with justification for each inclusion or exclusion (6.1.3)
- [ ] Set measurable security objectives (6.2)
- [ ] Build a legal, regulatory, and contractual register (A.5.31, A.5.34)

### Phase 2: Implement and Operate (Months 2–6)

**Clause 7: Support**
- [ ] P1: Competence records for key security roles (7.2)
- [ ] P1: Awareness program, onboarding training, and phishing simulation (7.3, A.6.3)
- [ ] P2: Document control procedure covering versioning, approval, and review cycle (7.5)
- [ ] P2: Communication plan (7.4)

**Clause 8 and Annex A:** see the top 10 in Section 3 and the mapping in Section 2.

**Additional Annex A gaps likely in your environment**
- [ ] P1: Cryptography and key management policy (A.8.24). This is also a PCI requirement.
- [ ] P1: Cloud service security (A.5.23)
- [ ] P2: Secure development lifecycle (A.8.25–8.29), since fintech products are likely built in-house
- [ ] P2: Separation of development, test, and production, plus protection of test data (A.8.31, A.8.33)
- [ ] P2: HR security covering screening, NDAs, joiner/mover/leaver, and remote working (A.6.1–6.7)
- [ ] P2: Physical security for offices and any server rooms (A.7.x), or an assurance report from your data center provider
- [ ] P2: Data deletion, masking, and data leakage prevention (A.8.10–8.12)
- [ ] P3: Threat intelligence (A.5.7)
- [ ] P3: Web filtering (A.8.23)

### Phase 3: Verify and Certify (Months 5–9)

- [ ] P1: Monitoring and measurement of the ISMS through KPIs and metrics (9.1)
- [ ] P1: **Internal audit** of all clauses plus a sample of Annex A controls, done by someone independent of the work, such as a contractor (9.2)
- [ ] P1: **Management review** with documented minutes (9.3)
- [ ] P1: Nonconformity and corrective action log, with findings closed (10.2)
- [ ] P1: Stage 1 audit (documentation review), followed by remediation
- [ ] P1: Stage 2 audit (effectiveness), about 4–8 weeks after Stage 1

### Mandatory Documented Information

Auditors will ask for each of these by name:
- Scope
- Security policy
- Risk assessment process and results
- Risk treatment process and results
- Statement of Applicability
- Objectives
- Competence evidence
- Operational planning records
- Monitoring results
- Audit program and results
- Management review results
- Nonconformities and corrective actions

---

## 2. Mapping Existing Processes to High-Priority Annex A Controls

| Existing process | Annex A controls | Likely gap | Action | Evidence auditors want |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ITIL service desk** | 5.24–5.26, 6.8, 5.16, 5.18 | Security events aren't triaged separately. Access requests lack formal approval and recertification. | Add a "security incident" category with severity criteria. Require manager and owner approval for access tickets. | Ticket samples, categorization rules, approval trail |
| **Change process (partially followed)** | 8.32, 8.9, 8.19, 8.31 | Changes bypass the process. Emergency changes aren't reviewed afterward. No configuration baselines. | Make the process mandatory with a defined standard-change catalog. Run a weekly bypass report. Do post-implementation review of emergency changes. | Change records, change advisory board minutes, exception reports, hardened baselines |
| **Partial CMDB / asset inventory** | 5.9, 5.10, 5.11, 5.12, 5.13 | Incomplete coverage. No owners. Doesn't cover SaaS or data assets. No classification. | Extend to cloud, SaaS, and data stores. Assign an owner to every asset. Apply a 3–4 tier classification scheme. | Inventory export, owner list, classification policy, reconciliation records |
| **Endpoint protection and EDR** | 8.7, 8.1, 8.16 | Coverage not measured. Alert triage ownership unclear. Servers and cloud workloads may be missed. | Produce a coverage report against the inventory. Assign alert SLAs. Write a mobile/BYOD standard. | Coverage dashboard, alert handling records, endpoint policy |
| **Nightly backups** | 8.13, 8.14, 5.29, 5.30 | No restore testing. RPO/RTO undefined. Immutability unclear. | Define RPO/RTO per system. Run quarterly restore tests. Keep an immutable or offline copy. | Backup policy, restore test reports, business impact analysis |
| **Ad-hoc vulnerability scanning** | 8.8, 8.20, 8.22 | No cadence, no remediation SLAs, no tracking | Scan authenticated, at least monthly. Set SLAs (e.g., critical in 14 days). PCI also requires quarterly internal and external ASV scans plus annual penetration testing. | Scan schedule, reports, remediation tickets, exception register |
| **Informal IR playbooks** | 5.24–5.28, 5.5 | No approved plan, roles, or regulatory timelines | Formalize the IR plan. Include the GDPR 72-hour breach notification, PCI 12.10, and customer contractual notification terms. | Approved plan, tabletop exercise report, incident log, lessons learned |
| **Supplier contracts without security SLAs** | 5.19–5.23 | No supplier tiering, no security clauses, no monitoring | Tier suppliers by risk. Add security clauses and GDPR Article 28 data processing agreements. Track PCI service provider compliance status. | Supplier register, due diligence questionnaires, contract clauses, annual reviews |
| **Informal policies** | 5.1, 5.36, 5.37 | Not approved, communicated, or reviewed | Build a policy set with approval, staff acknowledgment, and annual review | Signed policies, acknowledgment records, procedure documents |

---

## 3. First 10 Controls and Practices to Implement or Formalize

Ordered by certification dependency first, then risk.

| # | Control / practice | Reference | Why first | Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **ISMS scope, governance, and roles** | Clauses 4, 5; A.5.1, 5.2 | Everything else depends on this | Month 1 |
| 2 | **Risk methodology, assessment, and Statement of Applicability** | Clause 6.1.2–6.1.3 | The central certification artifact; drives which controls you implement | Month 2 |
| 3 | **Asset inventory and classification** | A.5.9, 5.12 | Risk assessment and access control both need it. You're already partway there. | Month 2 |
| 4 | **Identity and access management**: MFA everywhere, privileged access, quarterly access reviews, joiner/mover/leaver | A.5.15–5.18, 8.2, 8.5 | Highest-impact risk in fintech; required by PCI | Months 2–3 |
| 5 | **Incident management plan** with regulatory timelines and a tabletop test | A.5.24–5.28, 6.8 | Needed for GDPR and PCI; your playbooks give you a head start | Month 3 |
| 6 | **Vulnerability management** with cadence and SLAs | A.8.8 | Ad-hoc scanning is a likely major nonconformity and a PCI failure | Month 3 |
| 7 | **Enforced change management** | A.8.32, 8.9 | You have the process; it needs consistent operation and evidence | Month 3 |
| 8 | **Supplier security**: tiering, clauses, data processing agreements | A.5.19–5.23 | Contract changes take a long time, so start early. DORA flow-downs may land here. | Months 3–5 |
| 9 | **Logging and monitoring**: central logs, retention, time sync, alert review | A.8.15–8.17 | Auditors need proof that controls operate; PCI Requirement 10 | Months 3–4 |
| 10 | **Backup restore testing and continuity** | A.8.13, 5.29, 5.30 | Backups you haven't tested don't count as evidence | Month 4 |

**Next in line:**
- Awareness training (A.6.3). Start it in Month 2, because it needs time to accumulate records.
- Cryptography (A.8.24)
- Secure development lifecycle (A.8.25–8.29)

---

## 4. Indicative Timeline (9-Month Version)

```
M1  Scope, sponsor, gap assessment, select certification body
M2  Risk assessment, Statement of Applicability, core policies, awareness training launch
M3  IAM, incident response, vulnerability management, change enforcement
M4  Logging, backup testing, supplier work continues
M5  Secure development, crypto, HR controls; collect operating evidence
M6  Internal audit and corrective actions
M7  Management review, Stage 1 audit
M8  Remediate Stage 1 findings
M9  Stage 2 audit and certification decision
```

To compress this to 6 months, you would need a full-time ISMS lead plus external consultant support, a GRC tool for evidence collection, and Stage 1 booked by Month 4.

## 5. Risks to the Timeline

- **Resourcing:** Running this off the side of the IT manager's desk is the most common cause of slippage.
- **Supplier renegotiation:** Contract changes are slow. Prioritize Tier 1 suppliers.
- **Evidence gaps:** A control can be implemented but still fail the audit if there's no record of it operating. Start collecting evidence from day one.
- **Overlap with PCI:** Plan a single combined control set to avoid duplicate work.

# Part 1: Statement of Applicability Starter Sheet

## How to use it

**Full column set for your spreadsheet:**
`Control ID | Control name | Applicable (Y/N) | Justification | Implementation status (Not started / Partial / Implemented) | PCI DSS v4.0.1 ref | Cloud notes | Evidence | Owner | Target date | Risk IDs`

**Key rules:**
- **Every one of the 93 controls must appear.** Missing controls are a Stage 1 finding.
- **Justify inclusions too.** Link each to a risk, legal requirement, or contract. The "Risk IDs" column connects the SoA to your risk register.
- **"Not yet implemented" is not a reason to exclude.** Mark the control applicable and set the status to Partial or Not started.
- **Prefer "Applicable, inherited from CSP" over exclusion** for controls your cloud providers operate, such as data center physical security. Back them with the provider's attestations.
- **Defaults below assume** you have offices, develop software in-house, and run the cardholder data environment (CDE) in AWS. Adjust where wrong.

PCI references are to **PCI DSS v4.0.1** and indicate related requirements, not full equivalence. "—" means no direct PCI counterpart.
